blade.name: Tracer Blade
blade.lede: A blade for a stroke that arcs. Cut from one piece of 431 stainless, so what you feel at impact is the metal and nothing else.
gallery: The Tracer Blade in hand on the green
A putt dropping, shot from the cup
details: Fully CNC-milled 431 stainless steel, 3.5 degrees of loft at 35 inches, finished in gold. Toe hang suits a stroke that arcs back and through. Right hand.
One putter on the Lucky stock shaft with the Lucky stock grip. No head cover, which is why we sell one.
Orders leave in 1 to 2 business days. Sixty days from delivery on every club: contact us first, and it comes back in the condition it left in.

story.head: Fully milled, no inserts
body: Most putters at this price are cast and then given a face insert to make up for it. This one is fully milled from 431 stainless, which is slower to make and more honest to putt with: the feel at impact is the metal, not a softer layer hiding it.

It's a blade, so it suits a stroke that arcs. The toe hang does the job of squaring the face for you rather than asking your hands to. If your stroke runs straight back and through, the Mallet is the one to look at instead.

film: 16:9, 40 to 60 seconds. The head milled, then three putts rolled: a short one, a breaker, a long lag. Sound on for the strike.
blade.specline: Straight off the manufacturer's sheet. One length, one loft, one finish, because a putter does not need a menu.
blade.specnote: A blade this size wants a stroke with some arc in it. If yours is dead straight, the extra forgiveness on the Mallet is worth more than the shape.
quotes: The look alone is amazing!!! And I haven't putted this good in my life. I should have switched to blades years ago
I bought it because it's so pretty but it's a real step up from my old putter.
The quality and look on this putter is amzing . Everytime i play someone will ask where i bought it .

mallet.name: Tracer Mallet
mallet.lede: More forgiveness on the stroke most golfers actually have. Milled from one piece of 304 stainless, in both hands.
gallery: The Tracer Mallet on the green
The Mallet and two Lucky hats
details: Fully CNC-milled 304 stainless steel, 3.5 degrees of loft at 35 inches, finished in gold. Right hand or left.
One putter on the Lucky stock shaft with the Lucky stock grip. No head cover, which is why we sell one.
Orders leave in 1 to 2 business days. Sixty days from delivery: roll it on the practice green, and if it doesn't earn its spot, it comes back.

story.head: Built for the stroke you've actually got
body: A mallet pushes its weight out towards the edges of the head. Strike one off the middle of the face and it holds its line instead of leaking away, which is the entire case for the shape and the reason most golfers putt better with one.
The build is the same as the Blade: fully milled, no face insert, 3.5 degrees at 35 inches. What's different is the shape behind the face, and the fact that this one comes in both hands.

film: 16:9, 40 to 60 seconds. Head from above, alignment at address, then three putts: centre, toe, heel, all holding the line.
mallet.specline: Straight off the manufacturer's sheet. One length, one loft, both hands.
mallet.specnote: Same loft and length as the Blade. What changes is where the weight sits, and what that does to a putt you don't middle.

stryker.name: Stryker
stryker.lede: Titanium, with a flex channel behind the face. For the gap between the longest iron you trust and the fairway wood you don't.
details: Titanium head with a Flex Channel face and a Glide Sole, 19 degrees, 40.5 inches, on a stiff flex shaft. Face in brushed satin gold, sole in mirror gold, crown in gloss black with a gold starburst. Right hand or left.
One hybrid on the stiff flex shaft with the Lucky stock grip. No head cover, which is why we sell one.
Orders leave in 1 to 2 business days. Sixty days from delivery: take it to the range and the course, and send it back if the gap it fills turns out not to be yours.

story.head: The club that replaces the one you keep skipping
body: Everybody has a yardage they hate. Too long for the iron they trust, too short to bother with a wood, so they pull something they don't believe in and make a swing to match. Nineteen degrees covers that number, and a titanium head means the weight sits where it helps rather than in the material.

There's a flex channel behind the face, so a strike low on the face keeps more of its speed than it has any right to. The sole is shaped to glide rather than dig, which is what matters on the lies this club actually comes out for: thin ones, sat-down ones, and the rough.

film: 16:9, 40 to 60 seconds. Address view, face detail, then three shots: off the deck, out of the rough, and off a tee on a long par three.
stryker.specline: Straight off the manufacturer's sheet. One loft, one length, both hands.
stryker.specnote: Nineteen degrees sits where a 3 iron or a 5 wood would. If you carry both and trust neither, this is the club that ends the argument.
specs: Brushed satin gold face, mirror gold sole, gloss black crown with a gold starburst
quotes: Played 2 rounds and love swinging and hitting a fairway shot. Best club in my bag now
I'm loving my new hybrid. The gold color is stunning and the performance is unmatched. This club has replaced my sorry 3 wood.
I really like this hybrid. I'm still getting used to hitting it but I played it last night and what a beautiful sound it made when I struck it right!
